Reports the complement probability of the positive class
Flips the exponent sign, inverting the sigmoid

questions.stem: A naive Bayes classifier has class prior 0.3. Given two observed features, the class-conditional likelihoods for the positive class are 0.9 and 0.6, and for the negative class they are 0.1 and 0.2. What is the posterior probability of the positive class, to four decimals?

options.misconception: Uses a single likelihood and ignores the other evidence
Reports the prior and ignores the observed features
Reports the unnormalized numerator as if it were a posterior

questions.explanation: Naive Bayes multiplies likelihoods under the conditional-independence assumption: the positive score is 0.3*0.9*0.6 = 0.162 and the negative score is (1-0.3)*0.1*0.2 = 0.014. Computes entropy instead of Gini impurity
Reports purity, the complement of Gini impurity

Divides by one eigenvalue instead of the total variance

Adds a spurious five to the support of A
